description: Judge an RFC 6902 patch against the document it will be applied to. The patch is applied to a copy as a sequence, so each operation is judged against the state it will actually see rather than against the original: a later operation targeting a path an earlier one removed is the defect class this exists for. Reports a missing target, which makes the whole patch fail; a remove, which has no inverse; a replace that changes type; a move into itself; and a path the caller marked protected. Pay 150000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

document.description: The document the patch targets, as JSON text. Nothing is fetched: no cloud account is contacted and no credential is accepted, so the document supplied is the whole input.

patch.description: The patch, as a JSON array of RFC 6902 operations.

protected_paths.description: JSON Pointers that must not be touched. A path beneath one of these counts as touched.

name: json_patch_safety_audit

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

declares_test_operation.description: A test operation is how a patch refuses to apply to a document it was not written against.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

operations.description: Per operation: its op, path and whether its target existed at that point in the sequence.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

result_fingerprint.description: A hash of the resulting document, so a caller can confirm the outcome without the document being echoed back.

safe_to_apply.description: True only when every operation applies and none of them removes or retypes existing data. Not a judgement that the result is correct.

title: JSON Patch Safety Audit
